<!--
SHARED "YOUR OWN RECORDS" PANEL for every Data Explorer lesson — pull it into a lesson with Quarto's
include shortcode, naming this file (see the "Before we start" section of find.qmd for a working example).
It replaces the earlier pair of includes, _landings-data.qmd and _landings-guard.qmd, which put the fetch
and the data-frame conversion in front of the learner as two editable code boxes. Nobody in the audience
can read `tryCatch(as.data.frame(...))`, and nobody needs to: loading their own records is plumbing, not a
lesson. So all of it is hidden here, and what the learner sees instead is a status line and one button.

NOTE: do not write that shortcode literally in this file, not even inside a comment like this one. Quarto
resolves include shortcodes in a text pass that does not respect HTML comments, so a file naming itself
includes itself, and the render dies with "Maximum call stack size exceeded".

Six cells, in this order:

 1. `landings_state` (OJS, hidden) — fetches GET /api/data-download/explorer-data. This is the ONLY copy
    of the contract with the app: the localStorage keys `authToken` and `apiBaseUrl` (published by
    getApiBaseUrl in src/utils/axiosConfig.ts) and the endpoint path. Reading the base URL from
    localStorage is what lets a static lesson page reach the API exactly like the app does:
    dev -> http://localhost:3001/api, prod -> same-origin /api.
    It is a *generator* so the panel can show "getting your records" before the request settles, rather
    than leaving a blank gap that shifts the page when it fills. quarto-live's own webr-evaluate.ojs
    template does the same thing (yield a spinner, then yield the awaited result), so async generators in
    OJS cells are load-bearing in this extension already.
    Referencing `landings_reload` at the top is what makes the button work: OJS re-runs a cell when
    anything it reads changes, and Inputs.button counts its clicks, so each press re-fetches.
    The row cap comes back in the `X-Row-Cap` response header rather than being written here, so the
    number the panel quotes cannot drift from LESSON_ROW_CAP in api/data-download/explorer-data.js.

 2. `landings_rows` (OJS mutable) — the last rows that loaded SUCCESSFULLY, and the value the R cell
    consumes. `landings_state` writes it and nothing else does. It exists so a reload cannot briefly blank
    the data: read straight off the state, the loading phase would pass an empty array to the guard, the
    guard would rebuild `landings` as an empty frame, and a learner who pressed Run in that window would
    get an empty table for no visible reason.

 3. the status line — the only cell the learner reads. Written as a block with an early return per phase
    rather than a nested conditional, so each phase is named where it is handled.

 4. the button, and 5. a hidden cell that disables it while a fetch is in flight, because every press is a
    real PeSKAS call on a shared, rate-limited API key plus an audit row. Separate cell to avoid a cycle:
    `landings_state` already depends on the click count, so the button cannot also depend on the state.

 6. the guard (webr, `include: false`) — turns those rows into the data frame every lesson box calls
    `landings`. `include: false` evaluates the cell but shows no editor, no source and no output
    (live.lua ~line 121), which is exactly what plumbing wants. `autorun` is deliberately absent: with
    `edit: false` the block renders from webr-evaluate.ojs, which calls process() unconditionally —
    `autorun` is read only by the editor template, so setting it here would mislead the next author.
    When there is no data (not signed in, or the session has expired) it falls back to an EMPTY frame that
    still HAS the columns the lessons name, so the boxes below return an empty table instead of reporting
    a missing column — a message the learner would read as their own spelling mistake. If a lesson starts
    naming another column, add it here too.

The "not signed in" and "could not load" wording lives in the panel, not in R, so a learner who is not
signed in reads it immediately instead of waiting ~30s for webR to boot before R can print a warning.
-->

::: {.lesson-plumbing}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
landings_state = {
  landings_reload;

  yield ({ phase: "loading" });

  const token = localStorage.getItem("authToken");
  if (!token) {
    yield ({ phase: "signed-out" });
    return;
  }

  const apiBase = localStorage.getItem("apiBaseUrl") || "/api";
  try {
    const res = await fetch(`${apiBase}/data-download/explorer-data`, {
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, Accept: "application/json" }
    });
    if (!res.ok) {
      yield ({ phase: res.status === 401 || res.status === 403 ? "signed-out" : "failed" });
      return;
    }
    // The endpoint returns a bare array. Normalising anyway: `rows.length` is read straight into the
    // panel text, so anything else here would throw and take the whole panel down with it.
    const rows = await res.json();
    const safeRows = Array.isArray(rows) ? rows : [];
    // Absent on an older deployment; the panel then just omits the sentence about the cap.
    const cap = Number(res.headers.get("X-Row-Cap"));
    mutable landings_rows = safeRows;
    yield ({ phase: "ready", rows: safeRows, cap: Number.isFinite(cap) && cap > 0 ? cap : null });
  } catch {
    yield ({ phase: "failed" });
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
mutable landings_rows = []
```
:::

::: {.card .lesson-data-panel}
::: {.card-body}

```{=html}
<p class="card-title fw-semibold mb-2">Your own records</p>
```

::: {.lesson-data-status role="status" aria-live="polite"}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const s = landings_state;

  if (s.phase === "loading") return html`<div class="alert alert-light mb-0 d-flex align-items-center">
    <span class="spinner-border spinner-border-sm me-2" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    Getting your records&#8230;
  </div>`;

  if (s.phase === "signed-out") return html`<div class="alert alert-warning mb-0">
    <strong>You are not signed in, so there are no records to work with.</strong>
    The boxes below will still run, but they will come back empty.
    Open this lesson from the <strong>Data Explorer</strong> tab while signed in.
  </div>`;

  if (s.phase === "failed") return html`<div class="alert alert-warning mb-0">
    <strong>Your records could not be loaded just now.</strong>
    This is usually a connection problem, and nothing is wrong with your data.
    Press the button below to try again.
  </div>`;

  const capped = s.cap && s.rows.length >= s.cap;
  return html`<div class="alert alert-success mb-0">
    <strong>Your records are ready.</strong>
    ${s.rows.length.toLocaleString()} records loaded when you opened this page.
    ${capped
      ? html`That is the most a lesson loads. If you have more records, open the
             <strong>Data Download</strong> tab to get them all.`
      : html`They are the same records you can open in the <strong>Data Download</strong> tab.`}
  </div>`;
}
```
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof landings_reload = {
  // Inputs.button starts at 0 and counts clicks, which is all the trigger `landings_state` needs.
  // Its plain <button> is restyled to match the theme; guarded because a null here would break the cell
  // and the learner would lose the button altogether.
  const view = Inputs.button("Load my records again");
  const button = view.querySelector("button");
  if (button) button.className = "btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary";
  return view;
}
```

::: {.lesson-plumbing}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  // Nothing rendered — this only keeps the button in step with the fetch. See note 5 in the header.
  const button = viewof landings_reload.querySelector("button");
  if (button) button.disabled = landings_state.phase === "loading";
}
```

```{webr}
#| include: false
#| input:
#|   - landings_rows
landings <- tryCatch(as.data.frame(landings_rows), error = function(e) data.frame())

if (nrow(landings) == 0) {
  landings <- data.frame(
    landing_date = character(), gaul_2_name = character(), gear = character(),
    catch_taxon  = character(), catch_kg = numeric()
  )
}
```
